status_summary: The hiring and appointee elements are operative: skills-based assessments and disparate-impact changes are in place (see c03-05) and Schedule G, OPM guidance and political appointee counts show the appointee ranks growing (see c03-07). The evaluation and pay elements are partly done: OPM appraisal rules and the 2026-09-21 ratings memo are in effect, while the removal-side proposal was still open and pay changes are limited (see c03-03 and c03-04). The stage is derived from two implemented records (70 each) and two in_progress records (55 and 30).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14170 signed (published 2025-01-30): directs a federal hiring plan with technical and alternative assessments and an 80-day time-to-hire target.
OPM and the Domestic Policy Council issue the Merit Hiring Plan, including USA Hire validated assessments.
Executive Order 14317 creates Schedule G in the excepted service for noncareer policy-making or policy-advocating positions, with no numerical cap (published 2025-07-23).
OPM issues guidance directing larger performance awards toward top performers.
OPM Senior Executive Service appraisal and accountability rule published (effective 2025-10-15).
Executive Order 14356 requires strategic hiring committees led by agency leaders and sets a continuing rule on filling and creating positions (published 2025-10-20).
The Partnership for Public Service reports, with data through 2026-01-31, 1,835 Schedule C and 770 noncareer SES appointees, the highest Schedule C count in its historical table.

OPM and MSPB publish the proposed rule Promoting Employee Accountability (default 30-day improvement period, removal as default penalty for unacceptable performance); no final rule as of the sibling record check.
OPM final rule on General Schedule performance appraisal published (effective 2026-08-06).
OPM interim final rule removes references to the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures from its regulations.
OPM proposes a rule that adds Schedule G to the excepted-service regulations (comments due 2026-11-17).
OPM memo caps combined top-two appraisal ratings at 40 percent of each covered career population and steers at least 60 percent of FY2026 bonus pools to Level 4 and 5 performers.

title: Align federal hiring, pay and retention with taxpayers; add political appointees
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c03-03 is in_progress 55, c03-04 is in_progress 30, c03-05 is implemented 70 and c03-07 is implemented 70. The Foreword sentence is a general direction rather than a specific measure, and the pay element is only partly done, so the combined stage is in_progress 55. Implemented 65 is defensible given the weight of the hiring and appointee records. The appointee counts cited in c03-07 come from a Partnership for Public Service report and are not repeated here. Events were copied from the sibling records and not re-opened in this run; details of the March 2025 to 2026 rules should be read in those records.
